marker: # ref_size is the product length measured in the SCHU S4 assembly GCA_000008985.1 (AJ749949.2) by in
# silico PCR with these primers, outer primer edge to outer primer edge. The primers are Table 1 of
# Johansson et al. 2004 and reproduce one product per locus. The publication's Genomic location column
# prints the end coordinate abbreviated, giving only the digits that differ from the start
# (1886647-7109 means 1886647-1887109); the decoded span equals the measured product for 24 of the 25
# loci. Ft-M10 is the one that disagrees: its cell decodes to 646 bp against a measured 617, a
# difference that is not a whole number of 16 bp units, so it is either a real difference between this
# assembly and the sequence used in 2004 or a mis-stated end coordinate; the measured 617 is used.
# unit_length, ref_repeats and the repeat motif are now the published values of Table 2 of Johansson
# et al. 2004, which gives the repeat motif, its size in nucleotides and the copy number in strain
# SCHU S4 for all 25 markers, so every locus is callable on the published scale rather than a derived
# one. An earlier version of this scheme filled 16 loci with copy numbers derived from the reference
# and left 9 empty, and warned that a derived count could be offset from the canonical allele by a
# constant. The published table bears that out: the unit length is confirmed at every filled locus,
# but the derived count was wrong at eight of them, Ft-M2 4 against 5 derived, Ft-M3 25 against 21,
# Ft-M6 4 against 3, Ft-M14 3 against 5, Ft-M15 2 against 3, Ft-M16 2 against 3, Ft-M17 3 against 4
# and Ft-M18 4 against 5, because the arrays are imperfect and an exact motif count misses the copies
# the paper includes. Those counts are now the published ones, and a run on SCHU S4 returns the
# published profile with a residual of zero at every locus.
# patterns, the stored repeat motif used for the tandem cross-check, are kept only at the eight loci
# where counting the motif in the reference returns the published copy number: Ft-M4, Ft-M5, Ft-M7,
# Ft-M8, Ft-M9, Ft-M10, Ft-M20 and Ft-M21, stored as the rotation the array begins with. At the other
# seventeen the motif is left out, because the array is imperfect enough that an exact count would
# contradict the published number; the published motif is recorded in this comment instead. Motifs:
# Ft-M1 AAT, Ft-M2 TAAATA, Ft-M3 AATAAGGAT, Ft-M6 TTGGTGAACTTTCTTGCTCTT, Ft-M11 AATTATAAAT,
# Ft-M12 TAGCTTTTTT, Ft-M13 CTCCAGGACCAA, Ft-M14 TCATTA, Ft-M15 ATACTT, Ft-M16 TAAAAGTAAG,
# Ft-M17 TATTTA, Ft-M18 CATTAA, Ft-M19 TAAATTTCTCATA, Ft-M22 AAAAAT,
# Ft-M23 AAGTAGCATTGTCACGACCTCCT, Ft-M24 ATAAATTATTTATTTTGATTA, Ft-M25 GT.
# The unit lengths were also tested across strains. A locus keeps the same flanking length in every
# strain, so its product sizes must differ by whole multiples of the unit. The panel was amplified in
# 22 Francisella genomes whose identity was read from the assembly headers: nine subspecies tularensis,
# among them SCHU S4, three holarctica, one mediasiatica and nine novicida. In the 13 genomes outside
# novicida 19 of the 25 loci obey the rule. Six do not, and the test cannot say whether a unit is wrong
# or a flank has an indel; the published units stand. Ft-M19 fits the 30 bp holarctica deletion that the
# paper itself reports. Ft-M20 fits the roughly 200 bp insertion that Vogler et al. 2008 describe in type
# A.II isolates, which francisella_vogler_2008 splits off as Ft-M20B. Ft-M11, Ft-M22 and Ft-M24 have steps
# of 24, 19, and 5 and 16 bp, which are not multiples of the unit and are most simply indels in the flank,
# a reading not tested here. Ft-M8 is displaced, as described next. In novicida, the more divergent subspecies, seven loci
# break the rule, which is expected of a panel built on tularensis. A product off the unit grid comes out
# fractional and is flagged INTERMEDIATE and not rounded.
# Ft-M8 is displaced in four of the 13 genomes outside novicida. Its product lies at 8 to 17 kb in SCHU S4,
# the holarctica strains and the other tularensis strains, but at 325 kb in NIH B-38, 1857 kb in the
# mediasiatica strain FSC147 and 1871 kb in WY96-3418 and WY-00W4114. There the primers have selected
# another member of the repeat family described below, not the array they amplify in SCHU S4, so an Ft-M8
# allele in those strains is not comparable with the reference.
# The same test matches these loci to the other bundled Francisella scheme, whose names are the padded
# spelling of these, Ft-M02 against Ft-M2, and which took its copy numbers from this scheme's SCHU S4
# counts; those counts are the published ones above.
# Ft-M5, Ft-M7, Ft-M8, Ft-M9 and Ft-M10 share the reverse primer and one 16 bp repeat unit,
# TTTCTACAAATATCTT, at five unrelated positions, so they sample one repeat family rather than five
# independent loci. That oligo occurs 50 times in SCHU S4 inside a conserved element, so each product
# is selected by size alone.
